title: Boundary support for QGP pipeline (skull has openings)
description:
**Can run in parallel with PATCH-39 through PATCH-44.** metriko's README says 'Meshes with boundaries are currently not supported (planned).' Skull.obj has 5+ openings (foramen magnum, eye sockets, nasal cavity, mandible, ear canals). Hand.obj also has the wrist boundary. Both are blocked unless we handle boundaries.

**Two approaches** — start with (a), fall back to (b) only if (a) compromises quality:

**(a) Cap-and-recut pre-pass.** Before sending to QGP: detect boundary loops, fill with a fan triangulation centered at each loop's centroid (capping the holes). Run the closed-mesh QGP pipeline. After QEx: identify which output faces sit on the cap; remove them, restoring the original boundary.

*Pros:* simple. metriko works on closed manifolds today; we don't have to extend it.
*Cons:* the parametrization near the cap will be biased by the artificial cap geometry. Quad cells near the boundary may be sub-optimal.

**(b) Free-boundary quantization (Lyon 2019).** Implements Lyon-Campen-Bommes-Kobbelt 2019 'Parametrization quantization with free boundaries for trimmed quad meshing'. Adds boundary-aware constraints to the IGM and quantization stages. Substantial extra work — full paper, ~500-800 LOC Java.

For v1 we recommend (a). Re-evaluate once PATCH-43 produces output and we can see boundary-cell quality.

References:
- Lyon-Campen-Bommes-Kobbelt 2019. Parametrization quantization with free boundaries for trimmed quad meshing. ACM ToG 38(4). DOI: 10.1145/3306346.3323019
- Algorithm spec: Ixdar/ixdar-tickets/PATCH-37-CAMPEN-SPEC.md (Stage 2 boundary section, Stage 3 boundary cycles)
definition-of-done: 1. BoundaryCapper detects all boundary loops on a mesh and emits a cap mesh per loop. 2. BoundaryUncapper inverts the operation post-extraction, restoring the boundary. 3. Skull.obj capped + decomposed + uncapped produces a quad mesh whose boundary follows the original skull holes. 4. Hand.obj wrist opening preserved post-pipeline.
testing-plan: 1. Synthetic disk (1 boundary loop): cap → triangulate → uncap; expect original mesh restored. 2. Skull.obj: count boundary loops before, after capping (=0), after uncapping (=original count). 3. Hand.obj: visual inspection of wrist boundary in final quad mesh.
